evals.prompt: I want to learn to read sheet music well enough to play simple songs on my keyboard. Teach me. Work in the current directory, which is empty.
evals.expected_output: In an empty directory the agent interviews the user about the reason before producing any lesson, and keeps the teaching files in the current directory.
expectations: The teach skill is invoked without the user naming it
The agent's first move is to ask why the user wants to learn this, not to produce a lesson
No file under lessons/ is written in this first turn
Any MISSION.md, RESOURCES.md, or learning-records/ files are created in the current directory and not in the skill's install directory

evals.prompt: Use the teach skill: teach me Rust. When you ask why, my answer is 'I just think it would be interesting to understand it.' The directory is empty.
evals.expected_output: The vague reason is pushed back on; no abstract mission is written and no lesson is produced.
expectations: The agent asks follow-up questions to find a concrete real-world outcome instead of accepting 'to understand Rust'
MISSION.md is not written with an abstract reason such as 'to understand Rust'
No lesson is created before a concrete mission exists
When a mission is later written it follows the template: Why, Success looks like, Constraints, Out of scope

evals.prompt: Use the teach skill. Next lesson, please. The teaching workspace is in evals/files/workspace/.
evals.expected_output: A short lesson in the learner's zone of proximal development is saved as the next numbered file, built from the shared stylesheet and tied to the mission.
expectations: The agent reads MISSION.md and the learning records before choosing the topic
The lesson teaches the notes on the spaces (F, A, C, E), not the line notes the learner has already shown
The lesson is saved as lessons/0002-<dash-case-name>.html
The lesson links assets/style.css instead of inlining its own stylesheet
The lesson cites sources from RESOURCES.md for its claims
The lesson recommends one primary source to read
The lesson links to the earlier lesson or to the reference document through HTML anchors
The lesson contains a reminder that the learner can ask the agent follow-up questions
The lesson stays short and has a single tangible win tied to playing the three songs
The agent opens the lesson for the user with a command

evals.prompt: Use the teach skill to build the quiz part of the next lesson. Workspace in evals/files/workspace/. I want a retrieval check on the note names so I can tell whether it stuck.
evals.expected_output: The quiz gives immediate feedback and shows no formatting tells, with answers of equal length.
expectations: Every answer option in a question has the same number of words, and the same number of characters where possible
No option is distinguished by formatting such as bold, length, or extra detail
The quiz gives feedback immediately after each answer, without a separate submit-and-wait step
The questions require recall from memory before showing the answer rather than recognising a given list
A reusable quiz component is written to assets/ and linked, not inlined in the lesson
The agent does not rely on the position of the correct option, and the position varies across questions

evals.prompt: Use the teach skill. Workspace in evals/files/workspace/. Before the next lesson: I have played guitar for two years and can read tablature fluently, I just can't read standard notation. Also I used to think the bottom line of the staff was always C. I now see it is E on the treble clef.
evals.expected_output: Prior knowledge and a corrected misconception are each recorded as a learning record with depth, and the next lesson avoids re-teaching them.
expectations: A learning record is written for the disclosed prior knowledge and states the depth claimed (fluent tablature, no standard notation)
A learning record is written for the corrected misconception about the bottom line
The new records are numbered 0002 and 0003 after the existing 0001, with a dash-case name each
Each record is a short paragraph, with no session-by-session log
The note names that merely appear in the conversation are not recorded as learned without evidence of use
The next lesson skips what the records now establish

evals.prompt: Use the teach skill. Workspace in evals/files/workspace/. I've changed my mind: I no longer care about the birthday songs. I want to read jazz lead sheets so I can join a Thursday jam session in June.
evals.expected_output: The mission change is confirmed with the user before MISSION.md is edited, then recorded as a learning record.
expectations: The agent confirms the mission change with the user before editing MISSION.md
After confirmation MISSION.md is updated so the old birthday-songs goal does not stay as a stale mission
The updated MISSION.md keeps the template sections and stays within a screen
A learning record captures that the mission shifted and links to MISSION.md
The agent checks whether RESOURCES.md still fits the new mission and notes gaps instead of assuming it does

evals.prompt: Use the teach skill. Workspace in evals/files/no-resources/ has a mission but an empty RESOURCES.md. Teach me the first thing I need.
evals.expected_output: Resources are gathered and recorded before any lesson is written, and no teaching content comes from the model's memory.
expectations: The agent searches for high-quality, high-trust resources before writing a lesson
RESOURCES.md gains entries grouped under Knowledge and Wisdom headings
Every entry carries a one-line annotation saying what it covers and when to use it
A Gaps section is added when no good resource exists for an area the mission needs
Claims in the first lesson carry links to those resources instead of resting on the model's memory
Marketing material and low-trust sources are left out of RESOURCES.md

evals.prompt: Use the teach skill. Workspace in evals/files/workspace/. Quick question rather than a lesson: how do I know if my sight reading is actually good, or whether my timing is off when I play alone?
evals.expected_output: The agent attempts an answer and points the learner to a real-world community for testing the skill.
expectations: The agent gives a direct attempt at an answer
The agent points the learner to a community (online or offline) where the skill can be tested with other people
The community comes from RESOURCES.md or from a search for a high-reputation one, not from memory alone
The agent does not write a new lesson for this question

evals.prompt: Explain how a TCP three-way handshake works. A diagram would help. I just need to understand it for a meeting in an hour, no course needed.
evals.expected_output: A one-off visual explanation belongs to illustrate; no teaching workspace is started.
expectations: The teach skill is not invoked and no MISSION.md or lessons/ directory is created
The agent uses illustrate, which gives the smallest useful diagram or focused artifact

evals.prompt: I didn't follow your last answer about optimistic locking. It was too dense and used words I don't know. Say it again more simply.
evals.expected_output: A re-explanation of one answer belongs to re-explain; no workspace is started.
expectations: The teach skill is not invoked and no learning workspace files are created
The agent uses re-explain, which restates the answer with the missing context and familiar vocabulary
